GitHub #492 ('catt takes over Domoticz's port 9090/9091') is not a port-binding bug. catt never binds that port. The reporter's Domoticz spawns a shell script that runs catt, and Domoticz's listening socket lacks FD_CLOEXEC, so catt inherits the descriptor (confirmed by identical fd=82 across domoticz -> sh -> script -> catt in their 'ss -ltnp' output). The port stays bound while any catt process is alive, so the port symptom is really 'catt hung and never exited'. Two rounds of fixes therefore just bounded waits: f9380bb for discovery, rep-xrozx for controllers.py.

Closing inherited file descriptors at CLI startup was proposed as belt-and-braces and explicitly rejected by Stavros: it fixes another program's bug and is unusual behaviour for a CLI. Don't re-propose it.

Note that this class of report can never be fully fixed from catt's side: 'catt cast <local file>' runs an HTTP server forever by design, so it will always hold an inherited descriptor for as long as it runs. If the reporter comes back a third time, check whether their script switched away from 'catt cast_site'.

Issue #496: users try 'catt set_default -d <device>', but -d is a top-level group option only ('catt -d <device> set_default'). Accepting -d after set_default/set_alias/del_alias was considered and explicitly rejected by the maintainer (2026-09-24). The fix was full --help text on those commands plus an error message that shows the correct form. Rejected because it adds a second device-selection path only for these commands, unlike every other command, plus precedence rules when both are given.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
